**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 48, verses 4–6:**

{4} He, exalted is He, informs of His favour upon the believers in sending down tranquillity (al-sakinah) into their hearts. Tranquillity is calmness, peace of mind and steadfastness at the onset of distressing trials and difficult matters that unsettle hearts, startle minds and weaken souls. Among God's blessings upon His servant in such a state is that He makes him firm, steadies his heart, and sends down tranquillity upon him, so that he may receive these hardships with a steadfast heart and a tranquil soul, and thereby be prepared to uphold God's command in this situation. Through this, his faith increases and his certainty is perfected. When what occurred between the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the polytheists of those terms, whose outward appearance was a humiliation for them and a diminishment of their standing, which souls can hardly bear patiently, the Companions (may God be pleased with them) endured them; when they were patient with them and steeled their souls for them, their faith increased upon their faith. His words: {And to God belong the armies of the heavens and the earth} mean: all of them are in His dominion, under His management and subjugation. So let not the polytheists think that God does not support His religion and His Prophet. Rather, He, exalted is He, is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and His wisdom requires the alternation of days among people and the postponement of the victory of the believers to another time.

{5} {That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally, and remove from them their misdeeds}: This is the greatest of what the believers attain. That is, they attain what they desire and seek by entering the gardens, and He removes from them what they fear by expiating their misdeeds. {And that is, with God, a great achievement}: the reward mentioned for the believers. {With God, a great achievement}: this is what He does for the believers in that clear victory.

{6} As for the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, God will punish them for that and show them what grieves them, since their aim was to forsake the believers, and they harboured an evil opinion of God, thinking that He would not support His religion or exalt His word, and that the people of falsehood would prevail over the people of truth. So God turned their opinion back upon them, and the evil turn of fortune was upon them in this world. {God was angry with them}: because of what they committed of opposition to God and His Messenger. {And He cursed them}: that is, He removed them and distanced them far from His mercy. {And He prepared for them Hell, and evil is the destination.}

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 48, verses 8–9:

{8} That is: {Indeed, We have sent you} (O noble Messenger) {as a witness}, over your Ummah, concerning what they have done of good and evil; as a witness over statements and matters, as to what is true and what is false; and as a witness to Allah, Exalted is He, regarding His oneness and His being singularly perfect in every respect. {And a bringer of good tidings} to those who obey you and obey Allah, with the worldly, religious and otherworldly reward; {and a warner} to those who disobey Allah, with the swift and deferred punishment. Among the completeness of the good tidings and the warning is the explanation of the deeds and characteristics for which good tidings are given and warnings are issued; so he is the one who makes clear what is good and evil, happiness and misery, and truth from falsehood.

{9} For this reason, He ordained after it His saying: {that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger}; that is: because of the Messenger's call to you and his teaching you what benefits you, We sent him, so that you would establish belief in Allah and His Messenger, which necessarily entails obeying both of them in all matters, {and support him and honour him}; that is: that you support the Messenger (ﷺ) and honour him, meaning you magnify him, show him reverence, and fulfil his rights, as he has the great favour upon your necks; {and glorify Him}; that is: glorify Allah {morning and evening}: the beginning and the end of the day.

Thus in this verse Allah mentions the right shared between Allah and His Messenger, which is belief in both of them; the right specific to the Messenger, which is support and honour; and the right specific to Allah, which is glorifying Him and sanctifying Him through prayer or otherwise.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 48, verse 10:

{10} This pledge to which Allah referred is the Pledge of Ridwan (bay'at al-Ridwan), in which the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would not flee from him. It is a special contract, one of whose necessary requirements is that they not flee, even if only a few of them remained, and even if they were in a situation in which fleeing would be permissible. Thus Allah, Exalted is He, informed: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you﴾, the reality of the matter being that they ﴿pledge allegiance to Allah﴾, and make the contract with Him. So emphatic is this that He said: ﴿The hand of Allah is above their hands﴾; that is, it is as if they pledged to Allah and shook His hand in that pledge. All of this is for the sake of added emphasis and reinforcement, and to motivate them to fulfil it. Hence He said: ﴿Then whoever breaks [his oath] only breaks it to the detriment of himself﴾; that is, the burden of that falls back upon him and his punishment reaches him, ﴿And whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah﴾; that is, carries it out completely and fully, ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾, whose magnitude and worth none knows except the One who bestows it.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 48, verses 11–13:

{11–13} Allah, exalted is He, censures those among the Bedouin Arabs who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in jihad in His cause, whose faith was weak, in whose hearts was a disease and an evil opinion of Allah, exalted is He. They would make excuses, saying that their wealth and families had preoccupied them from going out in His cause, and that they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness for them. Allah, exalted is He, said: {They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts}. Their request for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness indicates their regret and their acknowledgment against themselves of the sin, and that they stayed behind in a manner that requires repentance and seeking forgiveness. If what was in their hearts had been this, the Messenger's seeking forgiveness would have been beneficial to them, because they had repented and turned back. But what is in their hearts is that they stayed behind only because they held a bad opinion of Allah, and they thought {that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families}; that is, they thought they would be killed and wiped out. This thought continued to be made attractive in their hearts, and they were at ease with it until it became firmly established. The cause of this is two matters. The first: they were {a corrupt people} (qawman bura); that is, ruined, with no good in them. Had there been good in them, this would not have been in their hearts. The second: the weakness of their faith and their certainty in Allah's promise, the victory of His religion, and the elevation of His word. For this reason He said: {And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger}; that is, indeed he is a disbeliever deserving of punishment, {so We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 48, verse 15:

{15} When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned those who stayed behind and blamed them, He mentioned that among their worldly punishments was that when the Messenger (ﷺ) and his Companions set out toward spoils in which there was no fighting, in order to take them, they [the stay-behinds] would ask to accompany them and join them, saying: ﴿Let us follow you﴾ — desiring by that ﴿to change the words of Allah﴾: in that He had decreed their punishment and the restriction of those spoils to the believing Companions, both by legislation and by decree. ﴿Say﴾ [to them]: ﴿You will not follow us; thus has Allah said before﴾: that you are deprived of them because of what you have brought upon yourselves, and because you abandoned fighting the first time. ﴿Then they will say﴾ in reply to this statement by which they were prevented from going out: ﴿Rather, you envy us﴾ — over the spoils! This is the extent of their knowledge on this matter. Had they understood what was right for them, they would have known that their deprivation was due to their disobedience, and that sins have worldly and religious consequences. Therefore He said: ﴿Rather, they did not understand except a little﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 48, verse 16–17:

{16} When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that the stay-behind among the Bedouin (al-a'rab) would remain behind from jihad in His cause, and would make excuses without a valid excuse, and that they would seek to go out with the believers when there was no military strength or fighting, but merely for the sake of booty, He said, testing them: {Say to the stay-behind among the Bedouin: "You will be called to a people of great military might; you will fight them, or they will submit."} That is: the Messenger, and whoever takes his place from the rightly-guided caliphs (al-khulafa' al-rashidun) and the imams, will call you. These people are Persia, Rome, and whoever resembles them or is similar to them. {You will fight them, or they will submit} means: either this or that. This is the actual situation: when they are in the state of fighting and combat against those peoples, if their strength and might are with them, then in that state they do not accept to pay the jizyah (poll tax); rather, they either enter Islam, or they fight over what they are upon. But when the Muslims overwhelm them, they become weak and humbled, and their might departs, so they become either those who submit (to Islam) or those who pay the jizyah. {But if you obey}: the one who calls you to fight these people, {Allah will give you a good reward}: that is the reward which Allah and His Messenger have set for jihad in the cause of Allah. {But if you turn away as you turned away before}: from fighting the one whom the Messenger called you to fight, {He will punish you with a painful punishment}. This verse indicates the virtue of the rightly-guided caliphs who call to jihad against the people of might among men, and that obedience to them in this is obligatory.

{17} Then He mentioned the excuses by which a servant is excused from going out to jihad, saying: {There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick}: that is, in staying behind from jihad because of their preventing excuse. {And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger}: in carrying out their command and avoiding their prohibition, {He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow}: therein is what the souls desire, and what the eyes delight in. {And whoever turns away}: from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, {He will punish him with a painful punishment}. So all happiness lies in obedience to Allah, and wretchedness in disobeying Him and opposing Him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 48, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

{29} God, exalted is He, informs about His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions, from among the Emigrants (Muhajirun) and the Helpers (Ansar), that they possess the most perfect qualities and the most exalted states. ﴿They are severe against the disbelievers﴾, meaning they are earnest and diligent in their enmity toward them, and they strive in that to the utmost of their ability, so the disbelievers found from them nothing but harshness and firmness. For this reason, their enemies were humbled before them, were broken, and were subdued by the Muslims. ﴿Compassionate among themselves﴾, meaning they love one another, show mercy to one another, and are tender toward one another, like one body, each of them loving for his brother what he loves for himself. This is their conduct with creation. As for their conduct with the Creator, you see them ﴿bowing and prostrating﴾, meaning their description is the abundance of prayer, the most important of whose pillars are bowing and prostration. ﴿Seeking﴾ through that worship ﴿bounty from Allah and His good pleasure﴾, meaning this is their aim: attaining the pleasure of their Lord and reaching His reward. ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration﴾, meaning the worship, through its abundance and excellence, has left its effect on their faces until they shine, since their inner selves were illuminated by prayer, so their outward appearance was illuminated as well. ﴿That﴾, the aforementioned, ﴿is their description in the Torah﴾, meaning this description with which Allah described them is mentioned in the Torah in this way.

As for ﴿their description in the Gospel﴾, they are described with another description: that in their perfection and mutual cooperation they are ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot and strengthens it﴾, meaning it sends forth its sprouts, and its sprouts support it in youth and maturity. ﴿Then it grows thick﴾, that crop, meaning it becomes strong and thick. ﴿Then it stands firm on its stalk﴾, the plural of which is saq (stalk). ﴿It pleases the sowers﴾ because of its perfection, uprightness, beauty, and balance. In the same way, the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, are like the crop in the benefit they give to people and in people's need of them. The strength of their faith and their deeds is like the strength of the roots and stalk of the crop, and the young and late-converted who joined the earlier and senior ones and supported and assisted them in upholding the religion of Allah and calling to it, is like the crop that sends out its shoot, which then strengthens it and grows thick. For this reason He said: ﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾, when they see their unity and their firmness in their religion, and when they clash with them in the battles of combat and the fury of war. ﴿Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward﴾. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who combined faith and righteous deeds, have been granted by Allah both forgiveness, whose necessary consequences include protection from the evils of this world and the Hereafter, and a great reward in this world and the Hereafter.

We shall relate the story of Hudaybiyyah in full, as it was related by the Imam Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim in al-Hady al-Nabawi, for in it is help in understanding this surah, and he has discussed its meanings and secrets. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Chapter on the story of Hudaybiyyah. Nafi' said: it was in the sixth year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah. This is the correct view, and it is the view of al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others. Hisham ibn 'Urwah said, on the authority of his father: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to Hudaybiyyah in Ramadan, and it was in Shawwal. This is an error, and the Conquest campaign was only in Ramadan. Abu al-Aswad said, on the authority of 'Urwah, that it was in Dhu al-Qa'dah, which is the correct view. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed four 'umrahs, all of them in Dhu al-Qa'dah. He mentioned among them the 'umrah of Hudaybiyyah.

He had with him one thousand five hundred. Thus it is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir. And on his authority in both: they were one thousand four hundred. And in both, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa: we were one thousand three hundred. Qatadah said: I said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: how many were those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan (bay'at al-Ridwan)? He said: fifteen hundred. I said: but Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said they were fourteen hundred. He said: may Allah have mercy on him, he erred; he told me that they were fifteen hundred. I say: both reports from Jabir are authentic, and it is authentically narrated from him that they sacrificed seventy camels (badanah) on the occasion of Hudaybiyyah, each camel for seven persons. He was asked: how many were you? He said: one thousand four hundred, with our cavalry and our infantry; that is, their horsemen and their foot soldiers. The heart inclines to this view, and it is the view of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Ma'qil ibn Yasar, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa' in the more authentic of two reports, and the view of al-Musayyab ibn Hazn. Shu'bah said, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father: we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree, one thousand four hundred. Whoever said they were seven hundred erred clearly, and his excuse was that they sacrificed seventy camels that day, and the camel has been permitted to count for seven and for ten. But this does not support what this speaker said, for he has stated that the camel in this campaign was for seven. So if the seventy had been for all of them, they would have been four hundred and ninety men, and he has said in the same narration itself that they were one thousand four hundred.

Chapter.

When they were at Dhu al-Hulayfah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) garlanded the sacrificial animals (hady) and marked them, and he entered into the state of ihram for 'umrah, and he sent ahead of him a scout from Khuza'ah to inform him about Quraysh. When they were near 'Usfan, his scout came to him and said: I have left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and they have gathered the Ahabish for you and assembled large forces, and they are going to fight you and bar you from the House. The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted his Companions and said: do you think we should turn toward the children of these people who assisted them, and take them captive? If they remain, they will remain bereaved and grieved, and if they are saved, it will be a neck that Allah has cut off. Or do you think we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we will fight him? Abu Bakr said: Allah and His Messenger know best. We came as those performing 'umrah, and we did not come to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then set out." So they set out, until when they were on part of the way, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with the cavalry of Quraysh as a vanguard, so take the right-hand path." By Allah, Khalid did not perceive them until he saw the dust of the army, and he set off running to warn Quraysh.

The Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded, until when he reached the pass by which they would descend upon them, his riding camel knelt down with him. The people said: "Hal, hal!" (a command to make the camel rise), but it refused. They said: "al-Qaswa has become stubborn, al-Qaswa has become stubborn!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "al-Qaswa has not become stubborn, and that is not her habit, but the one who stopped the elephant has stopped her." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honor the sacred rites of Allah, except that I will give it to them." Then he urged her on, and she sprang up with him, and he turned aside, until he halted at the far end of Hudaybiyyah, at a pool of little water, from which people only took small sips. The people soon drained it, and they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver, then commanded them to place it in the pool. He said: By Allah, the water kept welling up for them until they departed from it.

Quraysh were alarmed by his arrival among them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to send to them a man from his Companions. He called 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him, but 'Umar said: O Messenger of Allah! I have no one in Mecca from the clan of Ka'b who would be angered on my behalf if I were harmed, so send 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, for his clan is there, and he will convey what you desire. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and sent him to Quraysh, saying: "Inform them that we did not come for fighting, and that we came only to perform 'umrah, and invite them to Islam." He commanded him to go to men of faith and women of faith in Mecca, to enter upon them, to give them the good news of the conquest, and to inform them that Allah, mighty and majestic, will make His religion victorious in Mecca, so that faith will no longer have to be hidden there.

'Uthman set out, and he passed by Quraysh at Baldah. They said: Where are you going? He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sent me to invite you to Allah and to Islam, and to inform you that we did not come for fighting, and that we came only to perform 'umrah. They said: We have heard what you say; proceed on your errand. Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As stood up to him, welcomed him, saddled his horse, and set 'Uthman upon the horse; he gave him protection, and Aban rode behind him until he came to Mecca. The Muslims said, before 'Uthman returned: 'Uthman has reached the House before us and circumambulated it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not think he has circumambulated the House while we are besieged." They said: "What prevents him, O Messenger of Allah, since he has reached it?" He said: "That is my opinion of him: that he will not circumambulate the Ka'bah until we circumambulate with him."

The Muslims mingled with the polytheists regarding the matter of the truce. A man from one of the two groups shot a man from the other group, and fighting broke out. They exchanged arrows and stones, both groups shouted, and each group took its own people as hostages. It reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that 'Uthman had been killed, so he called for the pledge. The Muslims rushed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was under the tree, and they pledged to him that they would not flee. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own hand and said: "This is on behalf of 'Uthman."

When the pledge was complete, 'Uthman returned. The Muslims said to him: "Have you been satisfied, O Abu 'Abd Allah, with circumambulating the House?" He said: "Evil is what you thought of me. By Him in whose hand is my soul, even if I stayed there for a year while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained at Hudaybiyyah, I would not circumambulate it until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it. Quraysh invited me to circumambulate the House, but I refused." The Muslims said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most knowing of us about Allah, and the best of us in assuming good of others."

'Umar was holding the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the pledge under the tree, and the Muslims all pledged to him except al-Jadd ibn Qays. Ma'qil ibn Yasar was holding one of its branches, raising it above the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The first to pledge to him was Abu Sinan al-Asadi, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa' pledged to him three times, at the beginning of the people, in the middle, and at the end.

While they were in this state, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group from Khuza'ah, and they were the trusted confidants (aybat nasih) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among the people of Tihamah. He said: I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have settled at the watering places of Hudaybiyyah, with them the milch camels with their young, and they will fight you and bar you from the House. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We did not come to fight anyone, but we came as those performing 'umrah. Quraysh has been worn down by war and it has harmed them. If they wish, we will make a truce with them for a period, and they will leave me and the people alone. If they wish to enter what the people have entered, they may do so; otherwise, they will have gathered their strength. But if they refuse anything except fighting, then by Him in whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this affair of mine until my neck is severed, or until Allah makes His command take effect." Budayl said: I will convey to them what you say. He went until he came to Quraysh and said: I have come to you from this man, and I heard him say a statement. If you wish, I will present it to you. Their foolish ones said: We have no need for you to tell us anything about him. Their men of judgment said: Tell us what you heard. He said: I heard him say such and such. He related to them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said. 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi said: This man has offered you a proposal of right guidance, so accept it, and let me go to him. They said: Go to him! He went and began speaking with him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. 'Urwah then said: O Muhammad! Do you think that if you uproot your own people, you have ever heard of any Arab who destroyed his own family before you? And if the other outcome occurs, by Allah, I see faces and I see a rabble of people who are likely to flee and abandon you. Abu Bakr said to him: Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Shall we flee from him and abandon him? He said: Who is this? They said: Abu Bakr. He said: As for Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a debt you owe me, I would have repaid you for it. He kept speaking to the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever he spoke, he took hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was at the head of the Prophet (ﷺ), carrying a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached toward the beard of the Prophet (ﷺ), he struck his hand with the sheath of the sword and said: Take your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)! 'Urwah raised his head and said: Who is this? He said: al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah. He said: You treacherous one! Am I not still striving to atone for your treachery? Al-Mughirah had accompanied some people, killed them, and taken their property, then came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, I accept it; as for the wealth, you have no share in it." Then 'Urwah began to glance at the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his eyes. By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) never spat a mucus except that it fell into the palm of one of them, and he rubbed it over his skin and face. When he commanded them, they rushed to carry out his command; when he performed ablution, they nearly fought over his ablution water; when he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and they did not fix their gaze on him out of reverence for him. 'Urwah returned to his companions and said: O people! By Allah, I have been received by kings: Khosrow, Caesar, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions honor as the companions of Muhammad honor Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits a mucus, it falls into the palm of one of them, who rubs it over his face and skin; when he commands them, they rush to carry out his command; when he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water; when he speaks, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not fix their gaze on him out of reverence for him. He has offered you a proposal of right guidance, so accept it.

A man from the Banu Kinanah said: Let me go to him! They said: Go to him! When he came in sight of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who honor the sacrificial camels, so bring them out to him." They brought them out, and the people met him reciting the talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these people should be barred from the House. He returned to his companions and said: I saw the camels garlanded and marked, and I do not think they should be barred from the House.

Then Mikraz ibn Hafs stood up and said: "Let me go to him!" They said: "Go to him!" When he drew near to them, the Prophet ﷺ said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and while he was speaking, Suhayl ibn Amr arrived. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Your affair has become easy for you." Suhayl said: "Come, write a document between us and you." So he called the scribe, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." Suhayl said: "As for 'the Most Gracious', by Allah, we do not know what it is! Rather, write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' as you used to write." The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.'" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to." Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House nor fought you. Rather, write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am the Messenger of Allah even if you deny me. Write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah." Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "On condition that you leave us free to reach the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "By Allah, the Arabs will not say that we were forced under pressure. But that will be in the coming year." So it was written. Suhayl said: "On condition that no man from us comes to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." The Muslims said: "Glory be to Allah! How can he be returned to the polytheists when he has come as a Muslim?" While they were in that state, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl [ibn Amr] came, dragging his feet in his shackles, having come out from the lower part of Makkah, until he threw himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said: "O Muhammad, this is the first thing I stipulate you return to me." The Prophet ﷺ said: "We have not yet finalized the document." He said: "By Allah, then I will never make peace with you on anything." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Then permit him for me." He said: "I will not permit him for you." He said: "Yes, do so." He said: "I will not do so." Mikraz said: "Yes, we have permitted him." Abu Jandal said: "O assembly of Muslims! Am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come as a Muslim?! Do you not see what I have suffered?!" He had been tortured severely for the sake of Allah.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "By Allah, I have not doubted since I embraced Islam except on that day. So I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Are you not truly the Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Why should we accept humiliation in our religion, then return when Allah has not yet judged between us and our enemies?' He said: 'I am the Messenger of Allah, and He is my helper, and I will not disobey Him.' I said: 'Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes. Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'" Umar said: "I came to Abu Bakr and said to him what I had said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abu Bakr responded to him just as the Messenger of Allah had responded, and added: 'Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by Allah, he is upon the truth.'" Umar said: "So I did good deeds because of that."

When he had finished with the matter of the document, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Stand up, slaughter, then shave your heads." By Allah, not one man among them stood up, even when he said it three times. When none of them stood, he rose and entered upon Umm Salamah and mentioned to her what he had suffered from the people. Umm Salamah [said]: "O Messenger of Allah! Do you want that? Go out, and do not speak to anyone among them a word until you slaughter your camel and call your barber so that he shaves you." He rose, went out, and did not speak to any of them until he did that: he slaughtered his camel and called his barber, who shaved him. When the people saw that, they rose, slaughtered, and some of them began shaving others, until some of them nearly killed one another out of grief. Then believing women came, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: {O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them...} up to {and do not hold to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women}. So Umar that day divorced two wives he had while they were in polytheism; one of them was married by Mu'awiyah and the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah. Then he returned to Madinah. On his return, Allah revealed to him: {Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future, perfect His favor upon you, guide you to a straight path, and help you with a mighty help...} to its end. Umar said: "Is it a victory, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." The Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah! What about us?" So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: {It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers...} the verse.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Fath. All praise and grace belong to Allah.
May Allah's blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, his family and companions.
